assessment.summary: ABL1 is one of the most comprehensively validated drug targets in oncology, with 7 approved kinase inhibitors, over 5,000 IC50 entries in ChEMBL, and 85 high-resolution crystal structures including a best resolution of 1.03Å. The target is deeply characterised in the context of BCR-ABL1-driven chronic myeloid leukaemia and is supported by extensive recent literature. Druggability is unambiguously high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 63.4 (46% high-confidence fraction) suggests significant disordered regions in the full-length protein — however, crystallographic structures of the kinase domain are exceptional and this does not impact druggability assessment
Resistance mutation landscape (e.g., T315I gatekeeper) continues to evolve and may limit efficacy of existing approved drugs in some patient subsets
Allosteric binding sites beyond the ATP pocket and myristoyl pocket are less chemically explored relative to the canonical binding site
Role of ABL1 gain-of-function variants in non-CML contexts (e.g., CHDSKM syndrome) is an emerging area with limited therapeutic data
